message.content:
[ISSUE #1] [SEVERITY: Critical] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)]
Description: The "4 GB" text displaying the current memory allocation has a contrast ratio of approximately 3.5:1 against the dark background, failing the 4.5:1 requirement for normal text.
Impact: Users with visual impairments (e.g., low vision, color blindness) cannot distinguish the memory value, making it impossible to verify or adjust settings accurately.
Fix: Increase the text color brightness to achieve ≥4.5:1 contrast. For example, change the text color to `#FFFFFF` (white) or `#E0E0E0` (light gray) and verify with a contrast checker.

[ISSUE #2] [SEVERITY: Critical] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum)]
Description: The "Balanced" button in the Launcher Performance section has a contrast ratio of ~3.2:1 (green text on dark background), violating the 4.5:1 standard for normal text.
Impact: Users cannot read the selected performance mode, leading to confusion about current settings and potential misconfiguration.
Fix: Adjust the button text color to a brighter shade (e.g., `#FFFFFF` or `#E0E0E0`) to meet 4.5:1 contrast. Alternatively, use a lighter background for the button (e.g., `#2A2A2A` with `#FFFFFF` text).

[ISSUE #3] [SEVERITY: Critical] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast]
Description: The green toggle switch (for "Performance Boost Pack") has a 2.1:1 contrast ratio against the dark background, failing the 3:1 requirement for UI components.
Impact: Users with low vision cannot perceive the toggle state (on/off), risking accidental changes or inability to confirm settings.
Fix: Increase the toggle's contrast by using a brighter green (e.g., `#4CAF50`) or a darker background (e.g., `#1A1A1A`). Verify with a contrast checker.

[ISSUE #4] [SEVERITY: High] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap]
Description: The dropdown menu for "Performance Renderer" (currently showing "Sodium (+ Iris)") lacks a visible focus indicator, and its keyboard navigation (e.g., arrow keys) is not apparent.
Impact: Keyboard users cannot interact with the dropdown, violating accessibility standards and excluding users who rely on keyboard input.
Fix: Add a visible focus ring (e.g., `outline: 2px solid #4CAF50; outline-offset: 2px;`) to the dropdown when focused. Ensure `tabindex="0"` is set for keyboard accessibility.

[ISSUE #5] [SEVERITY: High] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 2.4.7 Focus Visible]
Description: The "Memory Allocation" slider (green handle) and numeric buttons (2, 4, 6, etc.) lack a visible focus indicator when tabbed to.
Impact: Keyboard users cannot identify which element is focused, leading to errors in adjusting settings.
Fix: Add a focus ring to all interactive elements. For the slider, use `outline: 2px solid #4CAF50;` on focus. For buttons, use `outline: 2px solid #FFFFFF;` or match the brand color.

[ISSUE #6] [SEVERITY: Medium] [FRAMEWORK: Nielsen] [CRITERION: 5. Error Prevention]
Description: The "Performance Boost Pack" toggle does not have a confirmation dialog or undo option for accidental toggling.
Impact: Users may enable/disable optimization mods unintentionally, with no way to revert without manually re-toggling.
Fix: Add a tooltip on hover explaining the action or a "Reset to Default" button in the section to allow easy recovery.

[ISSUE #7] [SEVERITY: Medium] [FRAMEWORK: LawOfUX] [CRITERION: Fitts's Law]
Description: The "4 GB" text next to the memory slider is too small (≈14px) and far from the slider handle, increasing interaction time for users adjusting RAM.
Impact: Users take longer to verify and adjust memory settings, especially on high-DPI screens.
Fix: Increase the text size to 16px and place it closer to the slider (e.g., right-align with the handle) to reduce target distance.

[ISSUE #8] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: Nielsen] [CRITERION: 8. Aesthetic and Minimalist Design]
Description: The "RAM for Minecraft (max ~80% of system)" subtext under "Memory Allocation" is redundant, as the slider already implies this constraint.
Impact: Visual noise clutters the interface, making it harder to scan key information.
Fix: Remove the subtext or replace it with a tooltip on the slider handle for on-demand information.

[ISSUE #9] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: LawOfUX] [CRITERION: Law of Proximity]
Description: The "Performance Renderer" dropdown label is misaligned with the dropdown (label is left-aligned, dropdown is right-aligned), breaking the perceived relationship.
Impact: Users may associate the label with the wrong control, causing confusion.
Fix: Align the label and dropdown horizontally (e.g., both left-aligned) or use a consistent spacing pattern (e.g., 16px gap) to reinforce their connection.

[ISSUE #10] [SEVERITY: Low] [FRAMEWORK: WCAG] [CRITERION: 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions]
Description: The "Performance Boost Pack" toggle lacks an explicit label (e.g., "On/Off") or description for screen readers.
Impact: Screen reader users cannot determine the toggle's state or purpose.
Fix: Add an `aria-label` to the toggle (e.g., `aria-label="Performance Boost Pack: Off"`) and ensure the text "Auto-install Fabric optimization mods..." is programmatically associated with the control.

[CATEGORY: VISUAL HIERARCHY & LAYOUT] PASS — no issues found.
[CATEGORY: COLOR & CONTRAST] Issues found (see #1-3).
[CATEGORY: INTERACTIVE FEEDBACK] Issues found (see #4-5).
[CATEGORY: FORM DESIGN] Issues found (see #4, #10).
[CATEGORY: NAVIGATION] PASS — no issues found.
[CATEGORY: LOADING & EMPTY STATES] PASS — no issues found.
[CATEGORY: ERROR HANDLING] PASS — no issues found.
